confidence_why: 3 independent first-hand descriptions agree (2 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_quote: Words then may be monosyllabic (/ʔê/ 'repair', /khwah/ 'lack') or disyllabic (/bɔnaŋ/ '24-hr period'). Disyllabic words are stressed on the main (second) syllable. No words have been found with the full POSCHWVF structure — POS and W slots are mutually exclusive except in a few reduplicated forms.

sources.citation: Bon, Noëllie. 2014. Une grammaire de la langue stieng, langue en danger du Cambodge et du Vietnam. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2. 646 pp. (HAL tel-03025620)
sources.quote: 'Un mot sesquisyllabique est réalisé avec la dynamique suivante : la syllabe faible est non accentuée et brève tandis que la syllabe principale est réalisée plus « longue », avec une accentuation forte et légèrement montante.' Word canon (C(C)(v)(C)).C(C)V(C); 25% of lexicon sesquisyllabic, 75% monosyllabic (corpus Bon09).

sources.quote: 'simple words can be monosyllabic or sesquisyllabic ... one weak syllable, which is light, with a non-phonemic vowel, and one main syllable which is heavy, with a phonemic vowel - with the stress falling on the main syllable.'
sources.note: Modern phonology article with an explicit English stress statement (stress on the main syllable, pp.23-24); independent second source to cite alongside Haupers.
